title: Make String Anti-palindrome
summary: Given a string s of even length n , define it as an anti-palindrome if for each index 0 ≤ i < n , the character at index i is not equal to the character at index n - i - 1 .
statement: Given a string s of even length n , define it as an anti-palindrome if for each index 0 ≤ i < n , the character at index i is not equal to the character at index n - i - 1 . Your task is to transform the given string s into an anti-palindrome by performing any number of swaps of any two characters. You can perform zero or more swaps. Return the resulting string. If there are multiple valid strings, return the lexicographically smallest one. If it is impossible to transform the string into an anti-palindrome, return "-1".
constraints: s has positive even length and contains lowercase letters.
Rearrange its existing characters so every mirrored pair contains different characters.
Return the lexicographically smallest valid rearrangement, or -1 when none exists.
hints: Sorting is lexicographically best; conflicts can only occur where the same high-frequency character straddles the midpoint.
Start sorted and swap the conflicting second-half positions with the earliest later different characters.
Locate the first character after the midpoint run; while mirrored values match, swap it into the current second-half position, or return -1 if unavailable.
Each repair uses the earliest possible larger character, preserves all earlier positions, and failure means one character occupies more than half the multiset.
